body:
Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." A new S&P 500 record is in sight as earnings put the rally to the test. SpaceX and Palantir take center stage, while oil slides on hopes for a US and Iran breakthrough. Plus, Redd Brown joins us on McDonald’s leadership shakeup, Bob Sloan of S3 says SpaceX is the "frothiest trade the market has even seen." Phantom CEO Jim Cantrell takes a deep dive into the space boom, and Goldman's Amanda Lynam joins us with [...] FUELING PROFIT GROWTH AT CATERPILLAR.
EARNINGS NEXT AS THE SHARES RALLY 9%. DANI: YOUDANI:
ARE WATCHING BLOOMBERG OPEN INTEREST. WE TRADED ALL-TIME
HIGHS AND WE WILL END THEIR IF WE CAN CLOSE AT THIS LEVEL. WE ARE WELL ABOVE ON THE S&P,
THE NASDAQ RAILING 2%. THE DOW JONES ALREADY TRADING
AT A RECORD 1%. BRENT CRUDE IS DOWN 4.6%,
EATING THE OVERALL SESSION AS YIELDS COME IN LITTLE CHANGED. MAYBE THE YEN IS MORE
INTERESTING THIS MORNING. NVIDIA, A GOOD DAY FOR THEM. [...] WE ARE STILL DOWN 4%, BUT WE ARE BASICALLY AT THE $80 MARK.
MORE OPTIMISM THAT SOME SORT OF AGREEMENT OR PLAN WILL BE PUT
FORWARD BY THE OMANIS IN QATARIS THAT WILL ALLOW A
SHORT-TERM AGREEMENT THAT GETS THE STRAIT OPEN.
10-YEAR YIELDS DOWN BY 3.5 BASIS POINTS.
LET'S LOOK AT THE OTHER MOVERS ON THE RADAR THIS MORNING.
WITH THAT IS NORAH. NORAH: LET'S KICK THINGS OFF WITH ON
SEMI, UP .1%. THE COMPANY BEAT ON REVENUE AND
EARNINGS. THE STORY HAS NOT CHANGED.

JUNE AND NOTHING CENTS. ABOUT 0.2% FROM ALL-TIME HIGHS.
LISA: YOU HAD A FREAK OUT MELTDOWN IN
THE TECH SECTOR, A BALL OF CASH SHIFTING FROM TECH TO HARDWARE
TO HYPERSCALERS AND BACK AGAIN, AND MAY BE TO EVERYTHING OTHER
THAN SOME OF THE FRONTIER MODELS. THEN YOU HAVE THE ACTUAL
EARNINGS WHICH HAVE BEEN INCREDIBLE.
86% OF S&P 500 COMPANIES THAT HAVE REPORTED EARNINGS THIS
QUARTER HAVE BEAT EXPECTATIONS, WHICH IS THE MOST GOING BACK
FIVE YEARS. IT GIVES YOU A SENSE OF WHAT [...] I THINK WE ARE IN THE MIDDLE OF AN EXCEPTIONALLY GOOD EARNINGS
SEASON. THIS MIGHT BE THE PEAK OF
EARNINGS. FOR ME, THE BIG TEST FROM THESE
MARKETS IS HOW SEVERE IS THE DROP GOING FORWARD?
ARE WE GOING FROM A 45% EPS GROWTH RATE YEAR OVER YEAR TO A
MUCH MORE STILL POSITIVE 20 PLUS NUMBER?
ARE WE GOING TO A MID SINGLE DIGITS NUMBER WHICH HAS
HISTORICALLY BEEN THE NORM AT THIS STAGE OF THE EXPANSION?
THAT IS WHERE YOU WANT TO BE MORE CAUTIOUS IN THE NEXT FEW [...] RALLY. CHIPS, SOFTWARE, TOO. WHAT IS HAPPENING? CAMERON:
WHEN YOU HAVE 33% OF THE INDEX, THE MAG SEVEN, UP 8.5%, THAT
DOES A LOT TO BOOST THE OVERALL MARKET BECAUSE WHAT WE WERE
SEEING OVER THE COURSE OF THE LAST COUPLE MONTHS IS WEAKNESS
WITHIN HYPERSCALERS OR BEING OFFSET IN OTHER PLACES.
THE FACT YOU WERE SEEING 70% OF NAMES IN THE S&P 500 TRADE
ABOUT THEIR MOVING AVERAGE WITH A FLAT INDEX, IT IS TELLING YOU
THERE IS THIS BREADTH UNDER THE SURFACE.

Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) surged more than 9% and 7%, respectively, ahead of their earnings reports after the bell. SpaceX was set to issue results as a public company for the first time. (Read our SpaceX earnings live blog here.)

The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) and broader iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) jumped a respective 7.3% and 6.8% as AI-tied stocks ARM Holdings (ARM), Marvell Technology (MRVL) and Sandisk (SNDK) soared between 11% and 17%. [...] The Irving, Texas-based firm posted adjusted earnings of $8.17 per share on revenue that increased 24% year-over-year to a record $20.54 billion. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha had expected $6.10 per share and $18.95 billion, respectively. [...] UBS analysts recently wrote that there “might be some natural pullback in the market in the near term” for Eli Lilly following its recent rally, but that they expect gains in the long term, along with an earnings beat and raised forecast Wednesday.

Read the full article here.

-Aaron McDade
